title: Outcome-first-stublog — weekly experiment + retro
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to keep OKR thinking outcome-first + record micro-experiments and weekly retros. Not polished; rolling notes.

High-level north star (personal): reduce my scope-level P95 cycle time for small runtime improvements from idea -> validated PR from ~9 days -> 4 days by end of Q2.

Current objective draft (personal OKR draft)
- Objective: Ship measurable throughput/latency wins that cut infra costs for small models without regressing quality.
  - KR1: 3 experiments that reduce per-token cost by >=10% on at least one production route (baseline: c5-small-prod).
  - KR2: Decrease median review-to-merge time for infra PRs I touch to <=24h for high-priority fixes.
  - KR3: Add 2 automations that catch quantization regressions before staging (unit tests / perf checks).

Notes on metrics I actually track (simple, hacky):
- weekly: count of PRs opened by me that landed in <1 week (target 4/week).
- experiments: delta in tokens/sec and cost-per-1000-tokens (quick calc in sheet).
- quality: percent of regressions flagged by perf tests (goal 0 regressions hitting canary).

This week's quick check-in (2025-02-03):
- wins:
  - Prototype batching-config tweak (RDW-3267) reduced median latency by ~8% in local sim; cost calc shows potential 7% win at 2k tokens.
  - Wrote first draft of a tiny perf-check github action that runs on model quantization PRs. Hooked to branch tests.
- blockers:
  - CI perf test is flaky on macos-agent; false positives slowing down inner loop. Need SRE sync to get stable env.
  - Need access to the dedicated-prod metric backfill to compute cost curves for the quantized variants (asked infra, pending).
- experiments to run next:
  1) Batching tweak A/B on canary route (small model) — measure P50/P95 and cost-per-1k tokens over 24h. (ticket RDW-3310)
  2) Enable KV-cache warmup heuristic on low-latency routes for short contexts (quick flag) — expect ~5-7% latency drop on 256-token requests.
  3) Extend perf-action to run a cheap micro-benchmark on PRs that touch kernels.

Retrospective notes (what's actually happening vs expectation):
- I keep overestimating how many experiments I can run in parallel. My cognitive switching cost is the limiter, not infra. Need to batch my experiment work into two focused days per week.
- Quick wins require pre-registered measurement plan. Every experiment that shipped had a 5-minute spreadsheet laid out; the ones without measurable plan stalled.

Mini action plan (next 7 days):
- Monday: stabilize perf-action (add retry + record artifact); pair with Amina for test harness (2h).
- Tuesday: schedule 30m SRE sync to fix macos-agent flakiness (calendar invite sent).
- Wed: run 24h canary for batching tweak RDW-3310; collect metrics and write short note.
- Fri: triage results and decide go/no-go. If go -> open rollout config and small PR template.

Risk log / failure modes to watch for:
- Regression in quality after quantization (words-to-watch: hallucination, coherence). Mitigation: add small eval set and a regression alert in Optimize dashboard.
- Observability gap: cost estimation relies on backfilled metrics. Mitigation: add a fallback estimation heuristic and tag experiments as "estimation-limited".

Personal micro-commitments (promises to self):
- Keep experiment notes <300 words and push them same day the run finishes.
- If an experiment is still inconclusive after 48h of good telemetry, archive and learn one explicit lesson.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should I move these personal metrics into a lightweight sheet that auto-calculates cost deltas? (Pros: less manual math; Cons: more upkeep)
- Can we de-risk the macos-agent by provisioning a dedicated runner for perf jobs? Cost tradeoff TBD.
- Who owns the observable mapping from model-variant -> cost-per-1k-tokens? (Product or infra?)

Random quick links I refer to often:
- Perf checklist template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/12873-outcome-first-playbook
- PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/890
- Current experiment ticket: JIRA RDW-3310

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short, but capture the lesson. If an item becomes cross-team, move to shared drive / product notes.

Timestamped log (quick):
- 2025-02-03 09:12: wrote batching note + opened RDW-3310
- 2025-02-04 15:04: paired with Amina to wire perf-action, flakiness discovered on macos-agent
- 2025-02-05 08:20: scheduled SRE sync, drafted measurement plan for canary

End.
